title: Throughput pocket journal - week sprint check & micro-OKRs
content:
Purpose and constraints:
- Short, portable checkpoint I can scan in <= 5 minutes every Mon/Wed/Fri.
- Focus on throughput (outcome tokens) and context switches, not raw hours.
- Micro-OKRs are 3-day cycles (Mon-Wed / Thu-Fri + next Mon) to keep experiments tight.

This week's 3-day micro-OKR (Mar 2 - Mar 4):
- Objective: Reduce per-ticket cycle time for small infra fixes from 2.5 days -> <= 1.25 days.
  - Key result 1: Complete 4 infra-fix PRs (non-blocking) with single-review-turnaround.
  - Key result 2: Decrease average reviewer wait from 18h -> 8h.
  - Key result 3: Document 1 checklist template to reduce back-and-forth.

Why this matters (one-liner): Faster small fixes frees up mental bandwidth for chunked deep work and reduces context switching penalty across the week.

Quick metrics (local measurements):
- Last 7 days: small-fix PRs merged: 3 (avg cycle 2.1d), reviewer wait avg 20h, interruptions per day (calendar+slack pings while actively coding): ~5.
- Goal by Mar 4: 4 PRs merged, avg cycle <=1.25d, reviewer wait <=8h.

Hypotheses I'm testing:
- H1: If I add a 2-line template and label PRs as "small-fix/fast-review", reviewers will triage faster -> lower wait time.
- H2: If I block Slack notifications during 90-minute focus windows (calendar busy), interruptions drop and cycle time shortens.
- H3: Pairing one Friday morning with a reviewer reduces rework and prevents second-review delays.

Planned experiments this cycle:
- Monday: create checklist template and apply to 2 outgoing PRs; add label; ping reviewers in PR body with TLDR.
- Tues: calendar blocks 9:30-11:00 and 14:00-15:30 with "no-notify" note. Track interruptions.
- Wed: schedule 30m reviewer sync for one high-uncertainty PR (pair review).

Tactical TODOs (quick-hit):
- [ ] Draft small-fix checklist template (template saved under personal snippets).
- [ ] Add "small-fix/fast-review" label to repo and write PR body snippet. (linked PR: see linked_artifacts)
- [ ] Update reviewer rotation note in team handbook with suggested 24h watch window for that label.
- [ ] Measure and log reviewer wait times in this doc end-of-day.

Daily micro-retro prompts (what I'll scribble each check-in):
- What went well with reviews?
- Biggest blocker (people/tooling/process)?
- One action for tomorrow (<=15 min).
- Did interruptions >2 break my focus windows? Yes/No + count.

Notes / fragments (scratch):
- Observed: When I add TL;DR + one-line test instructions in PR, the first reviewer comment tends to be a single thumbs or merge OK. Keep it.
- Observed: Calendar blocks reduce Slack pings by ~45% but not GitHub notifications. Consider "out-of-office" style preface in Slack during focus blocks.
- Idea: Create a weekly digest (auto) of small-fix PRs merged with time-to-merge and reviewer to encourage compact feedback loops. Could be a simple GH Action + small sheet.

Risks / friction to watch:
- Over-labeling -> label fatigue; keep label usage explicit and ephemeral (remove after week).
- Reviewer bandwidth hitting peak on Thursdays; schedule pair review earlier in week.

End-of-cycle quick log (to fill Mar 4):
- PRs merged count: ___
- Avg cycle time: ___
- Avg reviewer wait: ___
- Interruptions per day mean: ___
- One insight: ___

Bookmarks / references (one-liners):
- "Deep Work" 90-min focus windows -> higher throughput.
- GH Action idea: /scripts/throughput-digest -> prototype.
- Template snippet (to paste into PR):
  TL;DR: one-line summary
  Why: one line
  Test: how to verify quickly
  Label: small-fix/fast-review
  Ping: @reviewer-name (optional)

Mental anchor (short): "Ship small things fast so big things stay calm."

Next checkpoint: Wed Mar 3 (quick metrics) + Fri Mar 5 (full retro + update micro-OKR).

Unresolved questions:
- Best lightweight metric to track interruptions automatically? (Slack regex? calendar collisions?)
- Should I set reviewer "office hours" on team calendar or rely on labels?

End of pocket journal entry.

(Notes to self: keep this doc short, copy template to repo if experiment wins, then archive.)
